The '''Vahla''' were a nomadic, [[near-Human]] [[Species/Legends|species]] who roamed [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] in search of [[Vahla homeworld|their homeworld]]. They were tall and slender, and possessed cartilaginous skeletons, which gave them exceptional flexibility. All were [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]], and they were regarded as having a natural shrewdness. Many Vahla belonged to a [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark-side]] cult called the [[Ember of Vahl]], and all Vahla were expected to heed the dictates of the cult's central coven.

==Biology and appearance==
Vahla were tall, slightly built [[near-Human]]s. The [[Gender/Legends|males]] averaged two [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in height, and females were slightly smaller. Their physiology was largely similar to baseline [[Human/Legends|Humans]], with the marked exception that their skeletons were mostly composed of thick cartilage rather than bone; this unique adaptation gave the Vahla greater flexibility than baseline humanity. However, they were more physically frail than similar [[Species/Legends|species]].<ref name="Legacy Era Campaign Guide" />

The [[Color/Legends|color]] of Vahla skin varied, with dark gray and dusky brown marking the extremes. Their [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] were often pale blue, gray, or lavender, and their [[Hair/Legends|hair]] color ranged from black to gray to white, with both or all three colors sometimes being present simultaneously. Occasionally, Vahla were born with red hair; those so endowed were often regarded as having been blessed by the [[Deity/Legends|goddess]] [[Vahl]].<ref name="Legacy Era Campaign Guide" />

==Society and culture==
The Vahla were a nomadic people who were forever in search of their [[Vahla homeworld|lost homeworld]]. They were generally regarded as a naturally bright and shrewd. Their small economy was stoked by petty theft and limited-scale [[Pirate/Legends|piracy]], and, following the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]], by [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunting]].<ref name="Legacy Era Campaign Guide" />

All Vahla were [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]], and whether aware or not, had ties to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]]. Most Vahla were members of the [[Ember of Vahl]], a dark-side cult that worshiped Vahl, a goddess of fire and destruction. Though not all Vahla were members, all were expected to follow the orders of a six-priest central coven believed to have been "chosen" by the goddess. To show their faith and devotion, those [[Chosen of Vahl]] would inflict scars upon themselves. The Chosen consulted with Vahl through use of [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-[[Force power/Legends|empowered]] [[Farsight/Legends|farseeing]]. They also interpreted signs and portents, and made policy for the Vahla.<ref name="Legacy Era Campaign Guide" />

==History==
The ancient Vahla were dedicated to serving Vahl, who some believed to have been originally a [[Force Adept]] who led her people in the conquest of their now-lost [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]. They were regarded as twisted and decadent, and several thousand [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the [[Sith–Imperial War]] the cult was decimated by the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] in an attempt to quash their dark and destructive tendencies. Since then, the Vahla traveled [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] as nomads. Their bitterness and hatred toward the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] did not diminish with the millennia, and a number of Vahla helped the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] hunt down the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] during [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] purge of the Order. By [[130 ABY]], the [[Jedi hunter/Legends|Jedi-hunting]] tradition that began nearly a century and a half earlier continued as numerous Vahla served as independent bounty hunters.<ref name="Legacy Era Campaign Guide" />

==Vahla in the galaxy==
The Vahla were vagabonds, constantly plying interstellar space in an ongoing quest to locate their homeworld. They could often be encountered engaged in small-scale acts of piracy, in petty thievery, or in bounty hunting. Ember of Vahl cultists were also known for kidnapping and sacrificing individuals to their destructive goddess. The cult did allow non-Vahla Force-sensitives to join, but only after passing a number of dangerous, fiery tests to prove their faith.<ref name="Legacy Era Campaign Guide" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Vahla were mentioned in the [[2009]] [[Wizards of the Coast]] reference work ''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]''.<ref name="Legacy Era Campaign Guide" />
